content_html_sanitized:
Having never been in the military, I have always felt a special obligation to the veterans I have met over the years, especially to those who have been abandoned to suffer with their injuries, physical and psychological. Frankly, it is unbelievable, shameful, and really just absurd that they are still being denied full access to medical cannabis even today when an overwhelming majority of the American people support medical cannabis.

 

Who do our Representatives really “represent”?

Cannabis and Democracy: Who Are Our Leaders Following? It Ain't Us!

 

Presently, there may or may not be legislation before this Congress for something or other that may or may not do something or other about allowing Veterans Administration Doctors to say something or other about medical cannabis to veterans. And that is the way it has been since whenever. Pardon the sarcasm, but it is entirely appropriate.

 

It was considered a great victory when the VA doctors were no longer required to narc on their patients for using medical cannabis.

See

VA and Marijuana – What Veterans need to know

 

Let me suggest some articles from the MarijuanaNews archives to give you some perspective on what our government, our politicians, We the People, have done to our veterans just since I have been reporting on it.

 

From 1997

See The Drug War Is Politics by Other Means: Blackwater Gets Billions to Fight Narco-Terrorism. Buying Constituencies for the Drug War. Analysis by Richard Cowan

From 1999

See Veterans Administration Leads New Effort In Treating Pain.

That's Odd; The Prohibitionists Told Us That Pain Is Being Adequately Treated.

And

Montana Judge Confiscates Home Of Veteran Growing Medical Marijuana For Gulf War Syndrome

And from 2000

Disabled Vet and Wife Held at Gunpoint By Narks Who Seize Their Medical Marijuana Plants. In Washington State, Which Has A Medical Marijuana Law.

(Because the only doctor available to them was a V.A. doctor, they were unable to obtain the state required medical note of referral, as federally paid physicians refuse to participate in I-692 for fear of federal reprisal.)

And from 2005

Steve Tuck's Appeal to Canada. His Life and A Country's Honor Hang In The Balance.

(He was taken from a hospital emergency room with a catheter attached to a jail in the US after the police lied to the doctors.)

 

And from 2025

Veterans Who Fought for Our Freedom May Finally Get Medical Cannabis (Not yet)

And

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis

 

There are many more in the archives that you can find on the Search function at the top of the page. You may need a powerful anti emetic, but, even if you are a disabled veteran, you won’t be able to get cannabis from the Veterans Administration.

We could not make this up.
